1. OBTAINING VALID CONSENT:

Consent: Is a pt’s agreement for a health professional to provide care.

Type:

•Non – verbal like presenting arm to check B.P.
•Verbal.
•Written.

For a valid consent:

•Be competent to make the particular decision
•Have received sufficient information to make decision
•Not be acting under stress.

Competent or having capacity:

•Capacity consists of following:
-Ability to comprehend & retain information
-A belief in information given
-Ability to use information given to arrive @ a decision.
•A Pt may have the capacity to Consent to some decision but not others. A Pt’s capacity may vary with factors such as confusion, Panic, Shock, Fatigue pain/ Medication. But such factors may not automatically render a pt incapable of Consent.

Adults with Incapacity:

•Before making decision, you must:
1.Make care of women your 1st concern
2.Treat them as individuals.
3.Respect their dignity and not discriminate against them.
4.Support and encourage the women to be involved in decisions about their treatment and care as far as they want (and are able) too.

Adults with capacity:

•You must also consider:

Whether women lake of capacity is Temporary or permanent.

2.Which procedure/ option would provide overall clinical benefit.
3.Which option, including the option not to treat, would be least restrictive for future choices.

Advance decision/ Advance directive:

•Reflects a pt’s wish to refuse a particlar type of medical treatment or care if they become unable to make or communicate decision themselves.
•If valid for current situation => must be respected.

Verbal:

-Infront of chaperone.
-Must be documented.

Example:

1.Breast examination.
2.Presence of students during surgery.
3.Emergency procedures – CS, Assisted vaginal delivery 1st and 2nd degree perineal tear (3rd and 4th written if time allows).

Em – LSCS Assisted vaginal, 3rd/4th degree => Better

To go for written if time allows.

Written:

1.OPD procedures in Gynae.
2.Any procedure under local, regional or GA.
3.Multimedia Images:
-Laparoscopic findings, USG pictures, X – ray for teaching.
4.Removal of tissue for research/ testing where samples are not anonymized.

Example: Mrs X Histopath.

5.Analysis of fetus following fetal loss after 24weeks of gestation.
6.Storing gamets – legal advice HFEA & written Consent.

Consent nota Needed:

-USG in pregnancy.
-Images storing for pt record.
-Specific Consent for removal of tissue for H/P is not required (unless anonymized and used in record & residual sample).
-Retained tissues for education/ Teaching.

Unexpected Pathology:

⇨Unexpected pathology related to complaints.

Treatment can be performed (Appendicitis – I/O torsion).

⇨Complication of surgery that is life threatening proceed with corrective surgery.
⇨Unexpected pathology not related to complaint.

Don’t proceed like pain RiF – operated for appendicitis, I/O ovarian cyst => don’t remove

⇨Unexpected pathology – Biopsy can be taken if it doesn’t upstage the disease.
⇨Unexpected Ectopic – remove.
⇨Unexpected I/U pregnancy – reschedule operation.

 

Obstetrics:

•During pain – no Consent.
•In between contractions or epidural => can give Consent.
•Consent for sterilization not be taken during labor or S/S.

If already signed during antenatal Period => can be performed.

Gillick Competent:

-< 16 years’ may wish to give their Consent for treatment without parent’s knowledge => mature Minor.
-Refusal of Treatment: Overridden Parental Consent or court orders.

Professional Translator:

-If Pt not knows English, but should not be a relative.
-Gillick competent => TOP can be performed.

Fraser law:

-Covers Contracepation in mature minors.

Important Points:

•All women age 18 or over => Capacity to give Consent.
•Pt can withdraw Consent @ any time if so, procedures should be stopped as soon as possible.
•No body can Consent for a person who has capacity.
•Consent does not expire.
•Consent must be written only when the law require it.
•No place in law for next of kin to give Consent.
•Doctor must act only in best interest of women.

 

Unconsious Pt:

-Doctor in best interest.
-Refusal of blood by Jehovah’s witness – don’t give blood.

Fetus in context of Consent:

-Fetus has no rights.
-Women wishes => Respect her wishes.
-Newborn has own rights.

Motogomery Rulling:

•Doctors advisry role involves dialogue, The aim of which is to ensure that the pt understands the seriousness of her condition and anticipated benfits and risks of proposed treatmen and any reasonable alterative so that she can make an informed decision.
•Wound infection – need to be informed by doctor.

Bolam Test:

Which asks whether a doctor’s Consent would be supported by a reasonable body of medical opinion no longer applies to issues of consent, The law now requires a doctor to take reasonable care to ensure that the pt is aware of any material risk involved in any recommended treatment and of any reasonable alternative or variant treatment.

Example:

-Necrotizing Fasciatus after C/S (rare complications).

Bolam Principle Update:

Doctor must ask themselves 3 Questions

1.Pt knows about Material risk of treatment I am proposing.
2.Pt knows reasonable alternatives.
3.I have taken reasonable care to ensure that pt actually knows this.

Bolitho Modification:

Court is not bound to hold that practice is acceptable by virtue of a reasonable body of expert opinion whick supports it.

Caldicott Principles:

1.Justify the purpose for using confidential information.
2.Don’t use personal confidential data unless it is absolutely necessary.
3.Use minimal necessary confidential data.
4.Access to personal confidential data should be on strictly need to know basis.
5.Everyone with access to personal confidential data should be aware of their responsibilities.
6.Comply with law.
•Disagreement between minor and parent:

 

Courtrulling may be sought.

•Parants refuses treatment of life threatening condition of a girl.

-Treatment is recommended.
-Consider 2nd opinion if death is not immediate.
•Parents of minor disagree with each other.

 

Court involvement.

•TOP under 16 years’ – provide TOP.

Don’t tell to parents but encourage the girl to tell her parents

 

Sexual offence Act:

Age of Consent 16 years

Under 13 can’t give Consent.

< 12 years => male is guilty of rape.

< 13 years => Male is guilty of unlawful sexual offense.

13 – 16years => Male is guilty of unlawful sexual offense

Only male is guilty of an offense.

Big Gap of Age => 4 years.

1.Breast Exam = verbal Consent in presense of chaperone + document.
2.Straight simple perineal tear repair under L/A = verbal.
3.Excessive tear under L/A or regional

•Maternal capacity ACT.
1.Has condition impairing function of mind/ Brain.
2.Not able to understand, retain ad weigh the relevant information.
3.Not able to communicate decision.
